policy_title: Invest in early years education and childcare
stated: Invest £1.4bn per year in Sure Start Centres and, in negotiation with the sector, extend the offer of childcare to 35 hours per week from nine months, focusing on play-based learning.

source.quote: Green MPs will advocate: • For £1.4bn per year to be invested by local authorities in Sure Start Centres. • In negotiation with the sector, to extend the outgoing government’s offer of childcare to 35 hours per week from nine months.

bearing_set.reason: £1.4bn in Sure Start Centres and a play-based learning offer from nine months directly expands early-years provision and targets the attainment gap for disadvantaged children.
Extending a subsidised childcare offer to 35 hours/week from nine months materially enables parental (especially maternal) employment and earnings.
If the 35-hour offer is publicly funded, it reduces one of the largest household cost lines for families with young children, warranting a real cost-of-living verdict.
£1.4bn/year is a material recurring spending commitment; absent a stated funding mechanism, this bears on the funded-vs-borrowed indicator and the sustainability of the debt path.

membership_note: Four genuine bearings: O7 (the designed-for early-years education effect), O2 (childcare affordability as a household cost-of-essentials effect), O4 (childcare access as an enabler of parental employment and earnings), and O12 (a recurring £1.4bn/year obligation without stated funding). O13 and O14 were considered but the aggregate-growth and inequality effects are adequately captured within O4 and O7 respectively without adding separate non-negligible verdicts.
